sourcePath.role: Creates a real temporary UTF-8 file and readonly physical resource grant; calls the actual ProjectMemory.captureFile; asserts enabled registry flags remain false.
Creates real Store and ProjectMemory with a constructor-local enabled predicate; opts in the source thread. No file-access dependency replacement.
captureFile checks current physical grant, then awaits withResourceGrant and readBoundFile, revalidates ownership, and persists exact UTF-8 source/ref/private grant metadata.
withResourceGrant resolves the readonly grant, enters withPathGuard, revalidates it and calls the real bound reader.
The win32 guard branch spawns the fixed system Windows PowerShell executable with windows-path-guard.ps1, requires acquisition response, and awaits guard teardown.
readBoundFile uses a real readonly file handle, regular/single-link checks and bounded byte reads.

nativePathReview.executionBasis: The actual Windows test result and immutable unmocked source path together establish native guarded FILE capture execution. No per-process PowerShell event trace or PID receipt was collected.

provedBehavior: Exact UTF-8 source bytes, full FILE reference, source digest, captured sequence and private grant metadata.
Second capture reuses the immutable source without a new Store mutation.
Source detail returns the captured bytes while the file bytes, identity, size and mtime remain unchanged.
Removing the current resource grant denies fresh accepted recall, pinned source detail and recapture.
Replacing the physical file with identical bytes but a different identity denies the same operations.
A caller retaining the prior accepted candidate list is still excluded by a fresh source-availability check, with empty injection and SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE reason.
Rejected recapture leaves sequence and stored source rows unchanged.
limitations: These are three Windows source-integration cases using disposable test-owned FILE grants. They do not prove arbitrary project-directory grants, every filesystem/reparse configuration or installed-package execution.
The fixture uses synthetic account/model identifiers and constructor-local memory enablement. It does not activate either production memory flag.
No live provider calls, recall quality evaluation, model token usage or provider cost were measured.
This successful shard does not establish overall CI success. The separate installed-desktop job failed preflight and its retention scenario has not supplied execution proof.
Linux skips and compilation were not used as native execution evidence.
